definition: Recording a company's daily financial transactions.
business_context_example: Good bookkeeping turns year-end from a crisis into an afternoon.

definition: The main record holding all a company's accounts.
business_context_example: Every transaction ends up in the general ledger eventually.

definition: A single record of a transaction in the accounts.
business_context_example: One journal entry was posted twice, which explains the difference.

definition: To record a transaction in the accounting system.
business_context_example: Post the entry to March, not April, or the month won't close.

definition: An entry recording money going into an account.
business_context_example: Every debit needs a matching credit somewhere.

definition: An entry recording money going out of an account.
business_context_example: The credit side was 200 euro short, so we started there.

definition: The system where every transaction is recorded twice.
business_context_example: Double-entry is 500 years old and still the reason errors show up.

definition: The organised list of all accounts a company uses.
business_context_example: A messy chart of accounts makes every report harder to read.

definition: A report checking that debits equal credits.
business_context_example: The trial balance didn't balance, so nothing else could be trusted.

definition: To compare two records and make sure they agree.
business_context_example: We reconcile the bank account every Friday morning.

definition: Checking the bank statement against the company's records.
business_context_example: The bank reconciliation found a cheque nobody had recorded.

definition: A difference between two figures that should match.
business_context_example: There's a 48-euro discrepancy and I want to know why, not round it.

definition: To make the accounts agree and be complete.
business_context_example: She balanced the books before the holiday and slept properly.

definition: A report showing how long customer invoices have been unpaid.
business_context_example: The aged debtors report shows 12,000 euro over 90 days.

definition: A document reducing the amount a customer owes.
business_context_example: We issued a credit note for the two cancelled sessions.

definition: Money owed that will probably never be paid.
business_context_example: We recorded 1,800 euro as bad debt after the client dissolved.

definition: The work of making sure customers pay on time.
business_context_example: Credit control isn't rude, it's just consistent.

definition: Recording income or costs when they happen, not when money moves.
business_context_example: The December accrual covers the electricity bill that arrives in January.

definition: A cost paid in advance for a future period.
business_context_example: Annual insurance is a prepayment spread over twelve months.

definition: Spreading the cost of an asset over its useful life.
business_context_example: The van is on five-year depreciation, so 4,000 euro a year.

definition: Spreading the cost of an intangible asset over time.
business_context_example: The software licence goes through amortisation over three years.

definition: An amount set aside for a future cost that is likely.
business_context_example: We made a provision for the disputed invoice, just in case.

definition: Reducing the recorded value of an asset.
business_context_example: The old stock needed a write-down of 30%.

definition: Something a company owns and uses for years, like equipment.
business_context_example: The projector is a fixed asset; the bulbs are an expense.

definition: Something expected to turn into cash within a year.
business_context_example: Stock and unpaid invoices are both current assets.

definition: A debt that must be paid within a year.
business_context_example: The overdraft sits under current liabilities.

definition: An asset's original cost minus depreciation so far.
business_context_example: The van's net book value is 6,000 euro after three years.

definition: Working out what stock is worth in the accounts.
business_context_example: Inventory valuation changed the profit figure by 4,000 euro.

definition: Revenue minus the direct cost of what you sold.
business_context_example: Gross profit is healthy; it's the overheads that hurt.

definition: What is left after all costs are taken out.
business_context_example: Net profit was 41,000 euro, about 9% of revenue.

definition: Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation.
business_context_example: Buyers asked for EBITDA, not the profit figure we usually quote.
audio_text: E B I T D A
translation_bg: печалба преди лихви, данъци и амортизации

definition: The process of finalising the accounts for a month.
business_context_example: Month-end close takes four days, and we want it down to two.

definition: The end of a company's accounting year and the work it involves.
business_context_example: Year-end is December here, so January is the busy month.

definition: Internal financial reports used to run the business.
business_context_example: Management accounts go to the directors on the 10th of each month.

definition: The difference between a planned figure and the actual one.
business_context_example: The variance on marketing spend was 2,300 euro over budget.

definition: A department or area whose costs are tracked separately.
business_context_example: Each branch is its own cost centre, so we can compare them.

definition: Capital expenditure: money spent on long-term assets.
business_context_example: The new classroom fit-out is capex, not a running cost.

definition: Operating expenditure: the day-to-day running costs.
business_context_example: Software subscriptions moved from capex to opex.

definition: The record of what the company owes its suppliers.
business_context_example: Check the purchase ledger before you pay anything twice.

definition: The record of what customers owe the company.
business_context_example: The sales ledger shows six invoices raised this week.

definition: A small amount of cash kept for minor expenses.
business_context_example: Petty cash covers stamps and milk, not taxis to Sofia.

definition: Proof that a payment was made.
business_context_example: No receipt, no reimbursement. That's the policy.

definition: To pay someone back for money they spent.
business_context_example: We reimburse travel within one week of the claim.

definition: The record showing how a figure was arrived at.
business_context_example: Every adjustment needs an audit trail, even the small ones.

definition: The invoices and papers that prove an entry is correct.
business_context_example: The auditor asked for supporting documentation on twelve entries.

definition: Whether an amount is big enough to affect decisions.
business_context_example: A 30-euro error is below materiality, but we still fix it.

definition: The official rules for how accounts must be prepared.
business_context_example: The group reports under international accounting standards.

definition: The official accounts a company must file by law.
business_context_example: Statutory accounts are filed within nine months of year-end.

definition: Recording income and costs only when money actually moves.
business_context_example: Very small businesses can use the cash basis instead of accruals.

definition: To move a balance into the next accounting period.
business_context_example: The unused holiday provision carries forward to January.
